site.title: Ministries
site.tagline: How governments are organised, with sources for every figure
quality.a: Every counted ministry rests on a legal instrument
quality.b: Every counted ministry rests on an official publication
quality.c: At least one ministry rests only on a secondary source
countries.title: Each country's ministries
countries.lede: Pick a country to see its full list of departments: the official name as the government spells it, the areas each one covers, and the source behind it. Plus everything we recorded and did not count, with the reason.
countries.pendingNote: These {count} countries are part of the planned scope (the EU-27) and have no page yet. Their absence here is not an absence of ministries.
country.countedNote: The {count} departments that meet the definition. The headline figure is this list, counted.
country.notCountedNote: Recorded in the dataset and deliberately outside the figure, each with its reason. This is what lets the number be argued with rather than merely believed.
country.populationNote: Context, not a denominator: nothing on this site is divided by population.
country.historyNote: Each step is a structural change with the legal instrument behind it. Select one to see which departments were in force.
timeline.subtitle: {count} structural states on record since {from}
timeline.gapNote: The line breaks over periods that have not been documented yet. An empty stretch means nobody has checked it, not that the figure held steady.
timeline.incompleteNote: Where the line is dashed, departments are on record as having existed but are not counted here, so the figure is a floor rather than a count.
timeline.selectHint: Select another step in the chart to see the departments of that moment.
empty.noData: No data yet for this selection.
